description: Progress events of a session: an append-only log read by adaptive polling. Each event has a per-session `seq` (a decimal string) allocated under the session row lock, so the cursor never skips an event: `UPDATE generation_session SET last_event_seq = last_event_seq + 1 ... RETURNING last_event_seq` inside the transaction that writes the event, with UNIQUE (session_id, seq). A global bigserial would NOT work: its values are assigned before commit, so a transaction that took a lower value can commit after a poller already read a higher one and the event would be missed forever. Authority: docs/architecture/ai-generation-platform.md section 5. No token streaming, EventSource or WebSocket in v1; if a streaming endpoint is added later (p50 time to first block above 5 s), the event contract does not change.

storage.allocation: UPDATE generation_session SET last_event_seq = last_event_seq + 1 WHERE session_id = :id RETURNING last_event_seq, in the transaction that appends the event; the row lock serializes concurrent writers of one session
storage.whyNotBigserial: bigserial values are assigned before commit, so commit order can differ from value order and a poller could pass an uncommitted lower value

fields.events: Events with seq > after, ascending, at most limit.
fields.cursor: Decimal string: seq of the last returned event, or the request's after when events is empty. The client sends it as the next after.
fields.session: {state, rowVersion}: the session now, independent of the events returned, so a poll can stop on a terminal state.
fields.activeSteps: Steps currently READY, RUNNING or WAITING_EXTERNAL: {stepId, artifactId|null, kind, state, startedAt|null}. Drives 'writing' indicators; empty when nothing is active.

attrs.text: Index Scan читает только нужные страницы.

eventFields.seq: Decimal string, per session, strictly increasing and gap-free in commit order because it is allocated under the session row lock; the cursor is this value. Never reused.
eventFields.type: ARTIFACT_STATE | BLOCKS_APPENDED | MEDIA_SLOT_STATE | USAGE_UPDATED | SESSION_STATE. A client ignores unknown types.
eventFields.payload: Small (the log row is bounded; BLOCKS_APPENDED at most 32 KiB). Large content is read with getArtifact.

ARTIFACT_STATE.clientRule: On PROPOSED (and on any change of currentRevisionId) re-read the artifact with getArtifact.

BLOCKS_APPENDED.emittedBy: TEXT_DRAFT checkpoints, at most every 750 ms or at a block boundary

payload.generation: Artifact-scoped monotonic counter (not the step attempt): it increases whenever the draft restarts for any reason (retry, repair, regenerate). A higher generation than the one the client holds means: discard earlier blocks.
payload.startIndex: 0-based index of blocks[0] among the draft's top-level blocks.
payload.blocks: Already compiled native-v1 top-level block nodes, at most 32 KiB.

BLOCKS_APPENDED.clientRule: Draft blocks are a preview: their node IDs are provisional and can differ from the stored revision. The truth is getArtifact after ARTIFACT_STATE=PROPOSED. Reveal blocks with an ink animation of at most 600 ms; no event is a live region.

attrs.text: Index Scan читает только нужные страницы.

MEDIA_SLOT_STATE.emittedBy: every media slot transition in states.json

payload.errorCode: null or one of states.json artifact.mediaSlotErrorCodes

MEDIA_SLOT_STATE.clientRule: READY: the renderer resolves the asset through the media APIs; until then it shows the paper placeholder frame.

USAGE_UPDATED.emittedBy: every committed DEBIT or RELEASE of the session's reservation

payload.deferredUntil: null, or the UTC instant (next day start in Europe/Moscow) until which steps wait because the daily burst of debits is reached

polling.clientCadence: One loop per open session: 1 s while the tab is visible and a step is active; 5-15 s in the background; immediately on visibilitychange; stop when session.state is CLOSED, CANCELLED or EXPIRED.
polling.retention: Events are kept until the session is closed (or cancelled or expired) plus one day (architecture section 5) and are deleted with the session when the retention worker purges it. A request after that, or for a deleted session, is a 404 and the client reconciles with listSessions.
polling.ordering: Per session, seq order is the order in which the row-locking transactions committed (the lock serializes writers); two events of one transaction have consecutive seq values.
polling.idempotentReads: Reading the same cursor twice returns the same events (no consumer state on the server).
